meta.title: Your Bank Doesn't Have Your Money Sitting In A Vault. Here's Where It Actually Is.
meta.hook: When you deposit $1,000 in a bank, the bank doesn't just hold it. Most of it gets lent out.
meta.description: Under the fractional reserve system, banks are required to keep only a portion of deposits readily available and can lend out the rest to other customers as mortgages, auto loans and business credit. That lending is how the banking system creates most of the money circulating in the economy — deposits become loans, which become new deposits elsewhere.
